To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the method of geometrical acoustics, as developed in the first part of this paper, is a powerful and useful tool for the analysis of wave propagation and scattering in inhomogeneous media, and that the method is particularly well suited to the study of high‐frequency wave phenomena.

(1) the leading term in the high-frequency asymptotic expansion of the acoustic field produced by a line source over a plane interface is a plane wave, and (2) the leading term is a spherical wave for a point source.

The method of geometrical acoustics is extended to apply to diffraction, reflection, and refraction at a plane interface, and to the diffractive wave which appears in the problems whenever total reflection takes place.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general mathematical theory of wave propagation in inhomogeneous media.
the development of a new method for the analysis of the propagation of sound waves in a medium which contains a plane interface.
the propagation of weak spherical or cylindrical acoustic shock waves at interfaces between different media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the geometrical acoustics of the present paper is a very satisfactory method for the solution of many problems in acoustics and electromagnetics.

the method of this paper, when applied to a wide variety of wave propagation problems in the high frequency limit, gives asymptotic results in complete agreement with those obtained by much more laborious methods.
the present method of geometrical acoustics is a powerful and useful one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

geometrical optics, when applied to a weak shock wave in a medium which is not too dense, gives results in agreement with those of the exact theory to a high degree of accuracy for all frequencies, except those in the neighborhood of the cut-off frequencies.
geometrical acoustics is a very useful approximation to wave theory for the study of high frequency problems in acoustics and electromagnetics.
the results obtained in this paper are exact, and are the first results which have been given in the literature which are exact for the case of total reflection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now calculate the leading term in the asymptotic expansion of a wave field produced by an arbitrary distribution of sources in a homogeneous medium, in a finite number of steps.
the diffraction of sound from a cylindrical or spherical wave is very different from diffraction from a plane wave.
the method of geometrical acoustics can be used to study the reflection and refractions of shock waves and diffracted waves at plane interfaces and plane slabs.
